newsitem.title: USA: Motions argued in Ohio county investment fund suit.
newsitem.headline: Motions argued in Ohio county investment fund suit.

text.p: An Ohio state judge said on Wednesday he hoped to decide by the end of the year whether Cuyahoga County prosecutors could continue to represent the county in a lawsuit filed in the wake of the 1994 collapse of an investment fund called SAFE.

Six brokerage houses and a bank named as defendants in the civil suit asked the judge on Wednesday to disqualify the prosecutor's office because the head of its civil division will be required to testify about his part in the fund's contract-approval process.
Defendants' attorney Kenneth Bravo said in court the county had not produced needed documents. The defendants allege misconduct on the part of the prosecutor's office.
County officials said in testimony before visiting Judge Joseph Grigsby in Cuyahoga County Common Pleas Court, a state court, that they acted properly.
Local judges were disqualified earlier from hearing the case because their budgets were affected by countywide cut after SAFE (Secured Assets Fund Earnings) closed.

The investment pool had about $1.1 billion in assets. County commissioners shut it down in late 1994, citing what they called risky investment strategies after it suffered large paper losses amid rising interest rates.
The principal was returned to about 75 other local governments, but the county partially sold off its remaining highly leveraged portfolio at a loss of $114 million.
Former county treasurer Frank Gaul has appealed his 1995 conviction on a misdemeanor charge related to SAFE. A second official pleaded guilty and was fined.
In the suit, the county and state seek unspecified punitive and compensatory damages. They allege that the defendants were negligent and violated fiduciary duties.

The suit also alleges two defendants, McDonald & Co Investments and National City Corp's National City Bank unit, violated Ohio securities law anti-fraud provisions and made negligent representations.
The defendants have not filed a response in court but McDonald has said it believes the claims are without merit.

The other defendants are PaineWebber Group Inc, Dean Witter Reynolds, EVEREN Capital Corp's EVEREN Securities Inc (formerly Kemper Securities), Travelers Group Inc's Smith Barney Inc and Tucker Anthony Inc.
